answer: Concrete defense: vouching with decay. A new identity gains influence only when an established member signs its record with a quill drawn from that member's own staked capital, and that signature bends like a willow under load - its weight halves each time the same member vouches again. Hollow clusters spawned by one operator therefore exhaust their sponsor's credibility within a few clones, forcing the attacker to recruit genuinely independent vouchers, every one real capital and every one slashable once the cluster is exposed.
